blocks.text: CALAPAN CITY, Oriental Mindoro — The Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources (BFAR) and other regulators will conduct daily water quality monitoring in coastal waters of Odiongan after reports of fish mortality on Oct. 4 and 6. The monitoring program aims to establish baseline environmental data and determine possible factors behind the incidents, BFAR in Mimaropa said in a statement on Monday morning. During an interagency meeting on Oct. 9, BFAR’s Provincial Fisheries Office in Romblon organized monitoring activities with the Odiongan local government and marine agencies such as the Philippine Coast Guard and the PNP Maritime police.
